title: User Journey Mapping Techniques
description: Map user journeys to uncover edge cases, identify bottlenecks, and design systems that serve real user behavior patterns.

data.text: User journey mapping is the practice of tracing how different types of users interact with your system to accomplish their goals. In system design interviews, journey mapping prevents you from optimizing for the happy path while ignoring error states, long-tail workflows, and cross-user dependencies.

Start by identifying the primary user personas. For each persona, map the steps they take from system entry to goal completion. Include success paths, failure paths, and recovery paths. A good journey map reveals where your system needs caching, where it needs retries, and where it needs human escalation.

data.title: Journey Mapping Steps:
items: Identify key user personas and their goals
List every touchpoint with the system
Identify failure points and recovery flows
Highlight steps that require real-time guarantees

data.text: Consider a ride-sharing app with three personas: rider, driver, and dispatcher. The rider requests a ride, waits for matching, and tracks the driver. The driver receives requests, accepts rides, and navigates. The dispatcher monitors surge pricing and reallocates drivers. Each persona has unique latency requirements and failure modes.

data.caption: Rider journey flow
data.definition:
journey
    title Rider Requesting a Ride
    section Open App
        Launch app: 5: rider
        View map: 4: rider
    section Request Ride
        Enter destination: 4: rider
        Confirm request: 5: rider
    section Wait for Match
        Searching...: 2: rider
        Driver found: 5: rider
    section Ride
        Track driver: 4: rider
        Complete ride: 5: rider

data.text: Journey mapping naturally exposes edge cases that functional requirements miss. What happens when a driver cancels after matching? What if the rider loses connectivity during payment? What if surge pricing creates too many drivers in one zone and too few in another? Each edge case becomes a reliability or consistency requirement.

data.title: Interview Strategy
data.text: Draw the journey map first, then derive requirements from it. Interviewers remember candidates who think in terms of user outcomes rather than component lists.

terms.definition: A fictional character representing a user type with specific goals, behaviors, and pain points.
The default, error-free sequence of user interactions that leads to successful goal completion.
A scenario outside normal operation, such as network failure, concurrent edits, or invalid input.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Journey maps reveal requirements that functional specs miss
Map happy paths, failure paths, and recovery paths
Use personas to represent distinct user needs
Each edge case becomes a reliability requirement
data.takeaway: User journey mapping transforms vague requirements into concrete, testable system behaviors.
